question.:question/problem:
Given the function $y=8{x}^{2}-2\log_{6}x,$ find the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1.$ Give an exact answer.

The instantaneous rate of change at $x=1$ is
{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To differentiate a logarithm with base $a,$ we use the formula

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\log_{a}x)=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}a}.
$$

To find the instantaneous rate of change at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(8{x}^{2}-2\log_{6}x) \\  & =8\cdot 2x-2\cdot \frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}6} \\  & =16x-\frac{2}{x\operatorname{ln}6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(16x-\frac{2}{x\operatorname{ln}6})|}_{x=1} \\  & =16(1)-\frac{2}{1\cdot \operatorname{ln}6} \\  & =16-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}6}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:

question.:question/worked-solution:
To differentiate a logarithm with base $a,$ we use the formula

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\log_{a}x)=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}a}.
$$

To find the instantaneous rate of change at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(11-3\log_{6}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(11)-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\log_{6}x) \\  & =0-3\cdot \frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}6} \\  & =-\frac{3}{x\operatorname{ln}6}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1/\operatorname{ln}6$ is 

$$

\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5\log_{6}x-2\operatorname{ln}x+6{e}^{x}) \\  & =\frac{5}{x\operatorname{ln}6}-\frac{2}{x}+6{e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(\frac{5}{x\operatorname{ln}6}-\frac{2}{x}+6{e}^{x})\,|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{5}{1\cdot \operatorname{ln}6}-\frac{2}{1}+6{e}^{1} \\  & =\frac{5}{\operatorname{ln}6}-2+6\cdot e\,.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
To differentiate a logarithm with base $a,$ we use the formula

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\log_{a}x)=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}a}.
$$

To find the instantaneous rate of change at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2\log_{8}x-5\operatorname{ln}x+8{e}^{x}) \\  & =\frac{2}{x\operatorname{ln}8}-\frac{5}{x}+8{e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(\frac{2}{x\operatorname{ln}8}-\frac{5}{x}+8{e}^{x})\,|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{2}{1\cdot \operatorname{ln}8}-\frac{5}{1}+8{e}^{1} \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}8}-5+8\cdot e\,.\end{aligned}
$$
